newsitem.title: USA: NYC lost 2,900 private sector jobs in August -- report. [CORRECTED 15:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: NYC lost 2,900 private sector jobs in August -- report. [CORRECTED 15:15 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects month of report from June to August.)
New York City lost a seasonally adjusted 2,900 private sector jobs in August, according to the a report released Wednesday by city comptroller Alan Hevesi.
The total loss for the month was a seasonally adjusted 2,000 because the public sector gained 800 jobs, according to the report.
The changes in the private sector and the public sector do not equal the total change because of rounding, the report stated.
The city economy has now lost jobs for two months in a row. The July decline was a seasonally adjusted 3,800, but in July the private sector gained 4,600 jobs.
Sectors showing gains in August were restaurants, up 600; finance, insurance and real estate, up 500 and services, up 300.
The manufacturing sector had the biggest loss, 3,700 jobs. Social services lost 600 jobs.
The government gained 800 jobs, the city comptroller's report said.

Both the state and federal government continued to cut employees, but local government, which includes city government and agencies such as Port Authority of New York and New Jersey and New York State Metropolitan Transportation Authority, added 1,100.
The report is based upon the city comptroller's office seasonally adjusting data provided by the Department of Labor.
